CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.

Public Meeting Access
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications-Channel 19, Time Warner-Channel 24 (analog) or Channel 131 (digital) , and AT&T U-verse Channel 99. The video taping of meetings are maintained as a permanent record and contain a detailed account of the proceedings. Council meeting tapings are archived and available for viewing on the City's website.
Agenda Materials
A full City Council agenda packet including relative supporting documentation is available at City Hall, the Solana Beach Branch Library (157 Stevens Ave.), La Colonia Community Ctr., Fletcher Cove Lifeguard station, and online www.cityofsolanabeach.org. Agendas are posted at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Writings and documents regarding an agenda of an open session meeting, received after the official posting, and distributed to the Council for consideration, will be made available for public viewing at the same time. In addition, items received at least 1 hour 30 minutes prior to the meeting time will be uploaded online with the courtesy agenda posting. Materials submitted for consideration should be forwarded to the City Clerk's department 858-720-2400. The designated location for viewing public documents is the City Clerk's office at City Hall during normal business hours.
Speakers
Please submit a speaker slip to the City Clerk prior to the meeting, or the announcement of the Section/Item, to provide public comment. Allotted times for speaking are outlined on the speaker's slip for each agenda section: Oral Communications, Consent, Public Hearings and Staff Reports.
American Disabilities Act Title 2
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office (858) 720-2400 at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode
and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.

C.1.
West Side Highway 101 Improvements - Preliminary Design Review (File 0400-10)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution 2011-126:
a.
Providing direction on various design features of the Highway 101 West Side Improvements Project. These design features include, but are not limited to, specifying the type of crosswalk signal control to be used at mid-block crosswalks and the direction/type of angled parking.
b.
Approving the preliminary design of the Highway 101 West Side Improvements Project and authorizing the City Engineer to work with Nasland Engineering to prepare the final design and bid documents for the Project.
2.
Adopt Resolution 2011-127:
a.
Approving a reimbursement agreement with Santa Fe Irrigation District for design and construction of waterline improvements along Highway 101. As part of the reimbursement agreement, SFID will reimburse the City for all costs related to and arising from the design and construction of the waterline improvement and relocation project.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item. Mo Sammak, City Engineer/Public Works Director, presented a powerpoint (on file). He reviewed the background and the fiscal impact of the project and said that the project addressed streetscape and traffic calming. He said that the design team met with property and business owners to solicit feedback on the proposed design.
Larry Thornberg of Nasland Engineering (City’s Consultant) reviewed the logistics of the project which included wider sidewalks, meeting areas, more parking, mid-block crossings, storm drain system, bio retention, and median trees.
Pat O’Connor of Parterre Landscape Architects (City’s Consultant) reviewed the streetscape portion of the project including medians, planters, landscaping, and the themes for each of the gathering areas.
Council recessed the meeting for a break at 5:57 p.m. and reconvened at 6:13 p.m.
Peter House stated he had concerns with bicycle lanes and parallel parking. He stated that there were studies that compared diagonal and parallel parking and that he recommended back-end or front-end parking.
Douglas Alden stated as a bicyclist he did not agree with the data mentioned regarding reverse angle parking, that cities had successfully used reverse angle parking, and he recommended utilizing reverse angle parking in this project.
Council discussion ensued regarding mid-block crossings, flashing and audible beacons, push button activation, decorative poles, and raised platforms.
Council continued discussion regarding types of trees in the parkway and the median, consider water resistance, variation in heights that are in front of businesses, planting more trees, and replacing some of the existing trees that are not currently doing well on the rail trail.
Mayor Heebner explained that the funds for the project were being used from Transnet sales tax, that SANDAG bonded the project, and that the bond was being paid for with a portion of the Transnet receipts.
Council discussion ensued regarding whether to include a logo on the tree grates, various logos, reverse angle parking vs. front end angle parking, the buffer and sharrow bicycle lane, speed reduction, parking spaces, and advance warning signage.
The Council Standing Committee met with the Executive Director of the San Diego County Bike Coalition and presented the existing plans to solicit feedback on the proposed project. Comments received from the bike coalition were positive and they considered the proposed improvements as beneficial to cyclists. They were also fine with having front end parking.
Council made the determination to have front end parking.
Council continued discussion regarding design features, benches vs. seat walls and heights, adding more seating areas, areas for artwork, newspaper racks, signage, trees and tree grates.
Staff and the Council Standing Committee will be working with the consultants.
MOTION: Moved by Campbell and seconded by Nichols to adopt Resolution 2011-127 only and received direction regarding design features of the Highway 101 West Side Improvements Project.
Motion carried unanimously.
